coaching.headline: Kira took over from 25.7; before that, short-handed fights at 20.2 and 22.1 donated a Fangtooth and two towers.
coaching.team: We won this in the last seven minutes and nearly gave it away in the middle. The opening was ours: Greystone took first blood on Crunch at 3.7. We took Fangtooth at 11 and Mini Prime at 18. The leak was mid, where Argus was caught alone by Neon three times before minute 10, and the first of those deaths handed over their Fangtooth at 5. Then two fights went wrong for the same reason. Khaimera and Kira took a two-man fight at their Fangtooth at 20.2 and lost it 0-2; three of us fought at an outer tower at 22.1 and lost 0-3. Those two fights gave up a Fangtooth and two outer towers, with Greystone winning his lane and no kill or death credited to him in either; a shove-and-rotate there changes the count. The Genesis Core at 24 then went uncontested with all five of us alive. Kira ended it. Eight of her 14 kills came from the fight at 25.7 onward, and each won fight after that became Primal Fangtooth, Orb Prime, then the inhibitors. Ten towers to three. Next game: no fights at their Fangtooth before the offlane has rotated.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: The fight at 25.7. Kira was the only one of ours credited at an outer tower against Muriel, Neon and GRIM.exe, killed two of them before dying, and Primal Fangtooth followed at 27. Every fight after that was won. The stretch from minute 20 to 24 had been the game going the other way.
coaching.whatWorked: Closing. The three won fights from 25.7 on were cashed into Primal Fangtooth, Orb Prime and the Genesis Core, and the game ended ten towers to three.

perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Kira carried the close. Fourteen kills, three deaths and 48,265 damage to heroes, with eight of the kills coming from the fight at 25.7 onward, when she was the only one of ours credited against three at an outer tower and it went 2-1. The two deaths that hurt, at 20.4 and 22.1, were inside short-handed fights the team should not have started.
perPlayer.63523579-8bde-4b3c-bc1a-62ac12f76d52: Khaimera did the objective work and paid for it in bodies. Five deaths, three of them between minute 20 and 24, the stretch that handed over their Fangtooth and two outer towers, including the first death of the two-man fight at their Fangtooth. His 24,567 damage to objectives led the roster; three completed items was the fewest.
perPlayer.78f6b9bb-653c-46bf-bf03-b3669063b1e9: Greystone played the cleanest game on the roster. First blood on Crunch at 3.7, one death all game at 10.3, and 3 kills with 5 assists. He has no kill or death credited in either fight we lost short-handed, alive and ahead in lane for both. Whether the wave let him leave is not in the feed; the team's choice to fight before he rotated is.
perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Argus donated the early mid lane, then bought it back. Neon caught him alone three times before minute 10, and the first of those deaths handed over their Fangtooth at 5. From there he took five kills, two on Muriel.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Nothing to fix for Phase. Twelve assists on 25 team kills, 13 wards and 18,548 healing, each the most on our roster, and no death before minute 10. Her two deaths came inside fights, the fight at our Fangtooth at 10.2, even 2-2, and the fight at 27.5, won 4-1.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.text: Kira won the game from the fight at 25.7 on, eight kills in that stretch and 48,265 damage to heroes.

63523579-8bde-4b3c-bc1a-62ac12f76d52.text: Five deaths on three completed items, three of them in the stretch that handed over a Fangtooth and two towers.

78f6b9bb-653c-46bf-bf03-b3669063b1e9.text: One death all game and first blood at 3.7; the fights we lost were the ones where he had no kill or death credited.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.text: Three solo deaths to Neon before minute 10 gave away the early Fangtooth; five kills afterward bought the lane back.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.text: Twelve assists on 25 team kills with the most wards and healing on our roster; nothing to fix.

22.1.call: Do not take this fight. Three of us at an outer tower against Neon, GRIM.exe and Crunch with Greystone alive and ahead in lane and no kill or death credited in it; it went 0-3 and cost two outer towers within two minutes, and the Genesis Core at 24 then went uncontested with all five of us alive. Reset and fight five.

23.6.call: The right fight, taken the right way: four of us at an outer tower, won 3-1. The miss is what followed, since nothing was taken in the next 90 seconds. Push the tower while they are dead.

27.5.call: Won 4-1 with Kira taking three kills, then Orb Prime a minute later. This is how a won fight should end: the objective taken while they are dead instead of a reset to farm.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.build: Off the core and it held up. Tainted Rounds put a healing cut on a Muriel-shielded duo, and the fight at 25.7, won 2-1 with only Kira credited on our side, was won on this build. Solaris and Ashbringer would have added an empowered basic that heals and cooldown refunds on hit.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.eternal: Vermis with Serration and Melting Point rewards exactly what she did from 25.7 on, standing on one target through repeated basics, at the price of the wider item-stat boost a Demiurge build would give.

63523579-8bde-4b3c-bc1a-62ac12f76d52.build: Two of the three core items were there, and Void Helm in place of Basilisk was the right lean against Neon's 36,820 magical damage. The problem was count, not choice: three items completed against a Feng Mao with four, and five deaths while building them.
63523579-8bde-4b3c-bc1a-62ac12f76d52.eternal: Vermis fits a jungler whose whole kit is sticking to one target through the Cull stun, and the cost is the flat extra health Krix would have given a five-death game.

78f6b9bb-653c-46bf-bf03-b3669063b1e9.build: On core with Overlord and Aegis Of Agawar; the missing magic resist against a three-magical lineup never cost a death, so nothing to teach here.
78f6b9bb-653c-46bf-bf03-b3669063b1e9.eternal: Thraex with Savage Strikes and Ferocity fits a frontliner who marks one target and grows stronger the longer the fight runs, which suits his stasis-reset style better than the pure health of Krix.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.build: Two of three core items with Wraith Leggings on; the three early deaths came before any of it was online, so there is no build story here.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.eternal: Vesh with The Tenth Seal and Mind Rot adds a damage-over-time tick to each poke ability, the right fit for a mage who wins by landing Dread Nova and Ether Crystal from range rather than one burst combo.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Marshal and Enra's Blessing on core; nothing to teach here.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.eternal: The engine does not model support Eternals; the field runs Exarch on Phase, which turns her heals and link into attack speed for the carry.

threats: Chain-CC risk (1 hard-CC abilities, ~1.3s of lockdown): Crunch Right Crunch (knockup 1.25s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Heal-stacking: Muriel. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought 2 items of it.
Dive threat on our backline: Crunch. Assign peel for the carry and ward the flanks.
synergy: Little hard CC on our side — we can't force a pick. Play for poke/objectives and punish their cooldowns, don't flip coin-toss 5v5s.
We have sustain (Phase) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Mercy poke → stack Vengeance → Shadow Glide reposition → Purge ult
ourKits.winCondition: stack Vengeance and shred with the channeled Purge
ourKits.playWith: peel so she can channel Purge safely
ourKits.playAgainst: interrupt/CC her during Purge; punish her short dash cooldown

ourKits.combo: Ambush leap → Unleash AS → Cull stun, Invigorate to cleanse+heal
ourKits.winCondition: stick on one target, stun with Cull and out-sustain via Spirit Regen
ourKits.playWith: follow-up burst inside his Cull stun
ourKits.playAgainst: ANTI-HEAL is mandatory — it guts his whole kit; kite the leap and CC through Invigorate

ourKits.combo: Assault The Gates leap → Make Way armor shred → Sacred Oath empowered basic → Stone Forged Soul stasis ult
ourKits.winCondition: front-line aggressively and reset the fight with the stasis heal
ourKits.playWith: a team that fights while he soaks and stasis-resets
ourKits.playAgainst: don't waste burst into his stasis — wait it out; anti-heal cuts the ult heal

ourKits.combo: Dread Nova stun → Ether Crystal push/lift → Particle Shredder channel → Synaptic Obliterator beams
ourKits.winCondition: poke from max range and zone with the crystal
ourKits.playWith: a frontline to protect his stationary channel
ourKits.playAgainst: dodge Dread Nova; dive him during the immobile ult channel

ourKits.combo: Telekinetic Link an ally → Psychic Flare blind → Energy Lance → Hyperflux buff ult
ourKits.winCondition: buff a hyper-carry through the Link and Hyperflux for a teamfight
ourKits.passive: abilities heal her and her linked ally
ourKits.playWith: the strongest carry to Link and supercharge
ourKits.playAgainst: kill the linked carry, not Phase; break the link timing

enemyKits.combo: Reaping Dash → Hamstring slows → Safeguard spellshield → Earth Shatter execute
enemyKits.winCondition: trade with the spellshield up and execute low targets with Earth Shatter
enemyKits.passive: permanent power on unique hero takedowns
enemyKits.playWith: setup that holds a target for the execute
enemyKits.playAgainst: bait Safeguard's spellshield before committing the key CC

enemyKits.combo: Alacrity shield+AS → Consecrated Ground bubble → Reversal global save
enemyKits.winCondition: keep the carry alive with global shields and enable their damage
enemyKits.passive: abilities grant Sentinel to allies; on-hit bonus
enemyKits.playAgainst: she has no damage threat — dive her carry through the shields or pick her first

enemyKits.combo: Energy Shield block → Displacement Blast → Assault Mode → GTFO lockon ult
enemyKits.winCondition: out-trade with Pulsefire and the spell-shield, finish with GTFO
enemyKits.playWith: peel so he can free-cast in Assault Mode
enemyKits.playAgainst: bait Energy Shield, then commit; dodge GTFO's slow channel

enemyKits.combo: Forward Crunch gap-close stun → Right Crunch knockup → empowered Left Crunch, sustain via Re-Crunch
enemyKits.winCondition: all-in a squishy with the empowered combo and heal back through Re-Crunch
enemyKits.passive: post-ability empowered basic that refunds cooldowns
enemyKits.playWith: peel-stripping engage so he reaches the backline
enemyKits.playAgainst: peel/CC him off — without resets he's stranded; anti-heal blunts Re-Crunch

lines: Lead story: Damage well above normal. 1,508 hero damage a minute, more than 90% of Kira carry players this patch (37% of the team's). The damage came from Tainted Rounds, Ruination, Imperator.
Purge at rank 3: 105s base, about 80.8s by the end (23% shorter) from 30 ability haste: Ruination 10, Nuclear Rounds 20.
Kira dealt 48,265 hero damage, 37% of their team's, with +242 physical power from items.
Tainted Rounds (item): On Successful Basic Attacks: Reduce the Target's Healing by 45% for 3s. Deal (+10%) (+20%) Damage On-Hit. Increases by up to 100% as the Target's Health decreases.
Ruination (item): Upon successful On-Hit Attack: Apply a bleed that drains Mana by 30 (+8% Target's Max Mana) over 4s. Deals True Damage equal to 80% of the Mana Drained.
Imperator (item): Critical Strikes deal 30% more damage.
Nuclear Rounds (item): Based on Critical Strike Chance: Increase Ability Damage by 10-20%.
Pacifier (crest): Dash a short distance. Empower your next Physical Damage Instance within 3s. Deals 30 (+25%) Damage. Increased by 2.5x against Targets below 20% Max Health.
Marrow (Eternal): Heal for 6%/7%/8%/9% of damage dealt to Heroes, increased up to 15%/20%/25%/30% based on your Missing Health. (65% effectiveness for AoE attacks, 15% against monsters.)
Blood Bank (Eternal minor): Store 100% of Hero damage as charges for 3s. Gain 0.75% Lifesteal per 100 charges.
The Maw (Eternal minor): Basic Attacks deal 10% bonus True Damage to targets below 40% Max Health.
Siphoning Purge (augment): Purge Heals for 25% of its damage dealt to Heroes.

Sustain: 22% lifesteal; Terminus: On Overhealing from Lifesteal: Convert excess Healing into a Shield. Max Shield size: (+100%). The Shield slowly decays 15s after leaving combat.; Blood Bank: Store 100% of Hero damage as charges for 3s. Gain 0.75% Lifesteal per 100 charges.; 4,551 healing recorded.

Loadout augment Siphoning Purge: Purge heals you for 25% of its damage to heroes. Since you are slowed and cannot attack during Purge, this keeps you alive while you channel into a group. (game text: Purge Heals for 25% of its damage dealt to Heroes.) (changes Purge, 80.8s cooldown with their haste) Field: 48.7% in 2400 games, 28% of picks, level the hero-role's 49.3%.

Loadout Eternal Marrow: Heals you for part of your damage to heroes, more the lower your health. Mercy shots and Purge both deal heavy damage, so it keeps you dueling when low. (game text: Heal for 6%/7%/8%/9% of damage dealt to Heroes, increased up to 15%/20%/25%/30% based on your Missing Health. (65% effectiveness for AoE attacks, 15% against monsters.)) Field: 46.5% in 501 games, 6% of picks, below the hero-role's 49.3%.

Loadout minor Blood Bank: Recent hero damage turns into extra lifesteal. A Mercy plus Dusk burst makes your following basic attacks heal more. (game text: Store 100% of Hero damage as charges for 3s. Gain 0.75% Lifesteal per 100 charges.) Field: 46.7% in 407 games, 81% of picks, below the hero-role's 49.3%.

Loadout minor The Maw: Basic attacks deal extra true damage to targets below 40% health. It helps finish targets after Dusk detonates your Vengeance stacks. (game text: Basic Attacks deal 10% bonus True Damage to targets below 40% Max Health.) Field: 46.1% in 360 games, 72% of picks, below the hero-role's 49.3%.

Loadout crest Pacifier: A short dash that empowers your next physical hit, much stronger below 20% health. Dash, then Mercy or a basic to execute, and a kill lets you recast it. (game text: Adrenalize:  Dash a short distance. Empower your next Physical Damage Instance within 3s. Deals 30 (+25%) Damage. Increased by 2.5x against Targets below 20% Max Health. Killing a Hero within 3s allows Adrenalize to be recast for 6s.) Field: 51% in 5055 games, 59% of picks, above the hero-role's 49.3%.
Stack (Healing off the damage): 5 effects on one trigger: Terminus, Pacifier, Marrow, Blood Bank, Siphoning Purge.

Stack (Kept alive in fights): 5 effects on one trigger: Terminus, Pacifier, Marrow, The Maw, Siphoning Purge. Together they made staying in a long fight cheaper: more armor, shields or healing the longer it went.
Stack (Every basic attack set off): 3 effects on one trigger: Tainted Rounds, Ruination, The Maw.

The Eternal was part of it: Marrow (Blood Bank + The Maw) sits on the same triggers as the items (healing off the damage; kept alive in fights; every basic attack set off), so the same fights paid out in both damage and staying power.
Countered? 2 of the 5 players Kira killed built physical armor (Feng Mao, Crunch). Anti-heal on GRIM.exe, Neon. We killed Kira 3 times.
Copy it? Marrow (Blood Bank + The Maw): 45.5% in 332 Kira carry games, below the hero's 49.3%. It wins less than usual elsewhere: it beat us, not the field.
